svg.aria-label: How to write 好: 6 strokes · 5 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 好
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 好 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 好.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%A5%BD.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 好. Medians 1–3 draw 女 first: a bent stroke descends down-left and sweeps right without lifting, a separately started stroke falls down-left, and a separately started horizontal crosses left-to-right. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a horizontal turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical descends and hooks left without lifting, and a separately started middle horizontal crosses left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, 女-before-子 component order, all three joined turns, and five intervening pen lifts; Noto's 子 top turn is more angular and its vertical hook is flatter than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
svg.text: How it is written — 6 strokes · 5 pen lifts · 9 movements

This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
